about: Per-device lowering choices by scalar type. Thread box: one thread computes T lanes along a non-fastest axis, so a read that does not move along that axis is loaded once for all T. A row {cc, device, dtype, ...} applies on the device whose compute capability ("sm_61") and name match; T is 2..16. Without a matching row the defaults apply. They are the fastest thread box measured on a contraction over a shared axis (64 x 64 tables, 8192 samples, a Quadro P2000, sm_61): float64 T = 16 (5.08 ms against 10.55 ms without a box; 64 to 128 registers, no spills); float32 T = 8 (2.25 ms against 5.62 ms; T = 16 within 1 %). HAWK_BOX=0 in the environment builds without a box. Contraction: "gemm" (a recognised sum of products goes to a matrix multiply) or "direct" (it stays the kernel's own loop); a row may set it, the defaults are "gemm" for both scalar types. Select weight: what one add of a runtime-index store written as selects costs against an indexed access (hawk.emit.rtstore); 1.0 by default, 4.0 for float64 on sm_61 (Quadro P2000, FP64 rate 1:32). Its rows are keyed by compute capability alone and read through the arch the build resolved for its device targets, so a host-only build never probes. Block tile: a row may carry tile = {kind, SB, T, R, EB, smem}: kind BF stages a read invariant along a non-fastest axis, BT stages the row a clamped slot read gathers from; SB threads per block, T lanes per thread, R rows per block, EB steps per staged tile, smem bytes of shared memory; absent by default, so no block tile. "examples" is documentation the reader ignores: two block-tile rows measured on the same contraction (P2000), not active until a tile emit reads them.
